Subject: Fwd: Quantum Edge renewal — capacity playbook (notes from tech sync)

Forwarding notes from today's technical sync and our recommended renewal structure. Summary bullets below, full notes in attached playbook.

Notes / ask:
- Current baseline (today): 120 sustained QPS peak, 95th-percentile token response ~260, tail up to 600 tokens on heavy inference paths.
- Growth: customer provided forecast implies +30% QPS in Q3 and +20% additional the following quarter (conservative ramp). Stressed test shows that a single A100-equivalent GPU sustains ~18 QPS at 512 tokens with our current kernel selection and batching.
- Recommendation (preferred): Add 10 A100-equivalent GPUs into a reserved pool (bringing total reserved to 28 A100-eq) and keep an on-demand burst allowance of 6 GPUs. This supports projected QPS with ~25% headroom and keeps P99 for 512 tokens at ~420–480ms under continuous batching.
- Alternate (hardware efficiency): 6 H100-class GPUs (higher perf per card) if Quantum Edge is comfortable with H100 pricing and slightly different batching profiles.
- Term suggestion: 12-month renewal with an option to extend to 18 months at a 6% discount if they commit to the full ramp schedule. Pricing uplift is ~+22% for the reserved expansion (offset by unit-price reductions in extended term).
- SLA: propose 99.9% availability for the reserved pool with a P99 latency objective for 512-token inference; include automatic fallback to hosted model variants if reserved pool capacity is exceeded.

Deliverables attached: capacity playbook (recommended sizing, monthly ramp plan, test results) and a draft term sheet for legal. Key customer asks to resolve: final GPU family (A100 vs H100) and acceptance of stepped ramp.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the quick turn. Short answers and an updated final ask below. I've attached the updated term sheet (v3) that includes a cost comparison for A100 vs H100 and a month-by-month activation schedule.

SLA / Latency: Tessa validated that with an H100-backed reserved pool of 6 cards plus the 6 on-demand burst we can meet sub-400ms P99 for 512-token requests under your projected load (with continuous batching and the KV prefix cache tuned). For the A100-equivalent plan, to meet sub-400ms we'd recommend the 10-card reserved expansion we originally proposed.

Our recommended renewal structure (final):
- Term: 12 months (option to extend to 18 months at -6% if signed within 7 days).
- GPUs: Reserve 6 H100s (preferred) OR 10 A100-equivalent GPUs (alternate).
- Burst: 6 on-demand GPUs for traffic spikes.
- Ramp: Month 1 activate 40% of reserved pool, Month 2 activate 70%, Month 3 full activation. (Detailed schedule in attached sheet.)
- SLA: 99.9% availability for reserved pool; P99 latency objective as above depending on GPU family chosen.
- Pricing: H100 plan is +9% vs baseline; A100 plan is +22% vs baseline. Detailed per-month invoices in term sheet.

Next steps: if you confirm preferred GPU family and the term length, we'll send the DocuSign and lock capacity. I've included HubSpot and DocuSign links below.

Cheers,
